text: The Sons of Tuireann are heroes of an ancient Irish story. The long tale is the Oidheadh Chlainne Tuireann, the Tragedy of the Sons of Tuireann. It tells of the brothers Brian, Iuchair, and Iucharba, children of the great goddess Danu and of the obscure Tuireann, son of the god of poetry Ogma and of the craft goddess Étan. Their father's enemy was the clever Cian, known for winning the fair Eithne from her father Balor. Cian saw the armed brothers and changed himself into a pig. The brothers changed into dogs and hounded him nearly to death, then let him become human and killed him. Lugh, the son of Cian, demanded a heavy honor-price for the murdered father. Brian and his brothers performed seven impossibly difficult deeds. They failed at the eighth, and no choice lay before them: the eighth was beyond their strength, and Iuchair and Iucharba died, and Brian soon after. The tragedy became one of the Three Sorrows of Ireland.
